author: 5kO0
content:
CAR layout byte-equivalence locked in.

Implementation:
- ts-runner/index.mjs: new car_write_blocks op accepting { root: cid_str|null, blocks: [[cid_str, hex_payload], ...] } and yielding raw CAR hex via @atproto/repo's writeCarStream. Bypasses BlockMap so the test controls block order exactly.
- tests/differential.rs:
  - differential_car_layout_byte_equivalence — runs the full mst_corpus through Rust blocks_to_car and TS car_write_blocks (with Rust-side block iteration order pinned for both), asserts byte-for-byte hex equality across 6 fixtures (single, two_keys, dense_small, tid_shape, fifty_keys, mixed_collections)
  - differential_car_layout_byte_equivalence_no_root — None root variant, exercises the empty-roots-array CBOR header path the multi-fixture test never hits
- car_blocks_wire helper builds the JSON envelope from a (cid, &BlockMap) pair.

What this validates byte-equivalent: header CBOR (version=1, roots=[Cid|empty]), header-length varint, per-block (cidlen+bytelen) varint, CID byte encoding, payload concatenation. Block ordering itself is intentionally controlled by the test (BlockMap iteration order is an implementation detail and explicitly out of audit scope).

Verification: TS_RUNNER_READY=1 cargo test -p proto-blue-interop-tests --tests passes 22 tests including both new CAR layout tests; cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.
